sarah_acmeops: Hey team — since 04:00 UTC our production service is getting steady 429s from your API. Traffic pattern didn't change on our side, ~3k req/min to a single tenant key. Can someone triage?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Sarah. Can you paste a sample request id or a curl we can use to reproduce? Also which model + endpoint?

sarah_acmeops: Endpoint: POST /v1/completions, model: rw-large-v1, example request-id: rq_20260217_042312_aa7c. Here's a stripped curl we ran: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"ping"}'`

	response headers we see: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1800/min`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 164s` and body `{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}`

matt_oncall: Thanks — headers show RPM cap at 1800. You're hitting ~3000rpm which explains 429s. Two quick questions: is traffic coming from many clients (fanout) or a single host?

sarah_acmeops: All traffic originates from a small fleet of 4 hosts. Each host does a lot of short-lived connections, no deliberate retry jitter implemented.

jordan_platform: Pinged runtime to confirm tenant throttle config — looks like this tenant is on the "standard" RPM tier (1.8k/min) with a burst window that smooths to 3k over longer intervals. Short spikes >1.8k in a minute will 429.

alex_support: Actionable next steps for customer: 1) Add exponential backoff + full jitter on 429s, 2) Stagger cron/flush jobs so they don't align to minute boundaries, 3) Request a temporary quota bump if you need higher sustained RPM while we monitor.

sarah_acmeops: We already retry immediately on 429 with fixed 500ms backoff — looks like that might be amplifying. Can you confirm recommended retry behavior?

matt_oncall: Please switch to exponential backoff with jitter, limit concurrent in-flight requests per host (try cap 50), and respect `Retry-After` header if present. Quick pseudocode: `sleep = base * 2**attempt + random(0, base)` up to a cap.

jordan_platform: Also check client-side connection pooling: short-lived TCP/TLS sessions lead to bursty connection spikes. Reuse HTTP keep-alive where possible.

alex_support: I've opened support ticket SUP-5462 and requested a 24h temporary RPM increase to 4k for acmeops while they roll out fixes. Matt, can you validate there's capacity on the dedicated pool?

matt_oncall: On it. Quick note: we can grant a short surge while watching token utilization; but long-term we want them on either Dedicated or to implement smoothing + batching.

sarah_acmeops: Appreciate it. We'll implement backoff + connection reuse and push a canary in next hour.

jordan_platform: If they need immediate relief and are okay with potential cost, recommend switching to a dedicated capacity plan — no tenant-level RPM throttles there.

alex_support: Follow-ups: - Sarah to confirm canary results in 1h - Support to monitor X-RateLimit-Remaining and RTTs - Platform to confirm temporary bump and note changes in SUP-5462.

sarah_acmeops: Canary rolled out: per-host RPM dropped to ~900 after changes, 429s dropped to near zero. Thanks all. :tada: 

matt_oncall: Confirmed on our side: we're no longer seeing sustained 429s for acmeops. Will close temporary bump request after 24h if stable.

deploy-bot: Deployment acmeops/patch-2026-02-17 completed in prod (canary=10%). Logs: `throttle: 0.3% -> 0.01%`

alex_support: Great outcome. I'll update SUP-5462 with runbook notes (backoff + keep-alive + per-host concurrency cap) and mark as monitoring. Thanks everyone.
